mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Case Packer and a Case Erector?

acceptedAnswer.text: A case erector forms an open case from a flat blank, and a case packer loads products into that case. TRF supplies case erecting only as part of an integrated solution: TRFOnepack erects, packs and seals in one machine, and end-of-line projects include case forming and closing, so one partner answers for the flow from flat case to sealed case.

mainEntity.name: What Is a Drop Packer, and How Does Gravity Packing Work?

acceptedAnswer.text: A drop packer collates products above an open case and loads them through a controlled drop instead of picking each one with a robot. TRFDroppack uses this principle for pillow bags, pouches, VFFS and other flexible packages. It fits when the product tolerates gravity loading and the pattern repeats, which keeps mechanical complexity low and removes robotic end-of-arm tooling from maintenance.

mainEntity.name: How Many Products per Minute Can a Robotic Case Packer Run?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRFRapidpack, the robotic platform, is designed for applications of about 100 to 200 products per minute. TRF publishes application ranges, not machine speeds: actual capacity depends on the product, the pick tool, the pack pattern, the case and the infeed, and TRF engineering validates it for each line before the design is closed.

mainEntity.name: Does a Case Packer Need Vision-Guided Robotics for High-Mix Production?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only when product position varies. TRFRapidpack picks with vision-guided delta robots when products arrive in a random flow, and with indexed picking when they arrive in a controlled position. High-mix lines often benefit from vision because it removes mechanical re-orientation at every SKU change, while repetitive formats can run on indexed picking or gravity loading.

mainEntity.name: Can Case Packing Equipment Integrate With My Existing Palletizer and Conveyors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each TRF case packing platform can run standalone or integrate with conveyors, case handling, palletizing and intralogistics. TRFIntraflow carries sealed cases to a TRFCobot, TRFCompact or TRFSpeed palletizer, or to a custom palletizer, and interfaces with existing equipment are defined during project engineering.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical ROI of Switching From Manual to Robotic Case Packing?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no typical figure, because payback depends on your plant. The estimate compares the installed cost of the system with the annual savings: people packing cases by hand on each shift, shifts per day, local labor cost, the output the line gains when packing stops being the constraint and time saved at changeovers. A TRF Sales Engineer builds it with your data.

mainEntity.name: Who Supplies Case Packing Equipment for Food and CPG Manufacturers in the US?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRF serves food and CPG manufacturers across the United States with three top load platforms, TRFRapidpack, TRFOnepack and TRFDroppack, and can supply case packing, conveying and palletizing as one end-of-line system, with one partner responsible for engineering, execution and system integration.
